evidence.requirements: Almost every requirement is met. The start page shows title, date/time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (views.js:51, start.jpg). Each tasting has a 'Book <title>' link (views.js:60). The form has labelled Name/Email/Guests fields (min 1, max 8) and a 'Book' button (views.js:78-87). Seat limits are enforced (store.js:70-71). The confirmation shows the 'Booking confirmed' heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (views.js:95-101, confirmation.jpg: 2 x EUR 32 = EUR 64). /staff has a Password field and 'Sign in' button, and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (server.js:6). Bookings are grouped by tasting with Cancel buttons that free seats (staff.jpg, store.js:96). PORT defaults to 3000, storage is in memory, and the UI is in English. One requirement is only partly met: 'Invalid input is rejected with an error message next to the form'. In form.jpg the invalid email is still in the field and no message is shown, because type="email" required (views.js:82) makes the browser block the submit with a temporary native popup. The server-side error box (views.js:67-68) never appears in normal browser use.
evidence.correctness: Validation is done in one place (store.js:60-86). Guests must be a whole number 1-8 (regex at store.js:16). The seat check counts current bookings, and an exact fill is allowed (store.test.js:58-67). Name and email are trimmed and checked. Cancelling deletes the booking, so seats are counted again from the remaining bookings (store.js:48-57, 96). createBooking is synchronous, so two simultaneous requests cannot both pass the seat check. Unknown tastings and references return 404 (app.js:86,121). The form re-shows the values that were typed (app.js:100). Minor: cancelling an unknown reference silently redirects (app.js:144). A fully booked tasting still shows a Book link and only fails on submit.
evidence.security: All output goes through escapeHtml (views.js:3-11), and a test checks this for the staff page (app.test.js:267-277). The password check hashes both sides with SHA-256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual (app.js:59-65), and login is refused when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset (app.js:60). Session tokens are 32 random bytes, stored server-side with an 8-hour expiry, in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (app.js:67-71,138). Cancel requires a session (app.js:143). The body is capped at 8 KB (app.js:6,17). Pages send a strict CSP, nosniff and no-store (app.js:42-44). No secrets are in the code. Gaps: no rate limit on login attempts, no sign-out, no CSRF token (SameSite=Strict largely covers this), and no Secure cookie flag (the README notes this).
evidence.code_quality: The code is small and split cleanly: store.js holds data and rules, views.js the HTML, app.js routing, sessions and auth, and server.js startup. Functions are clearly named (parseGuests, validateContact, seatsMessage, withSeatsLeft). Errors are handled in one place: 413 for oversized bodies and 500 with logging (app.js:151-161). There is no needless abstraction, and createApp takes the store and password as arguments, which keeps it easy to test. Comments are few and useful (store.js:5, app.js:56,61).
evidence.tests: There are 14 store tests and 18 HTTP tests (node --test) covering every brief requirement. They check the listing text, 'Book <title>' links, form labels with min/max and the Book button, the confirmation heading, total and reference, seats decreasing after a booking, and rejection when there are too few seats, including exact fill and the singular 'seat' message. They also cover invalid guests (0, 9, 2.5, text, empty), invalid email and name, the staff login form, wrong password, unset password, grouping and ordering, cancel freeing seats, cancel without auth, XSS escaping and the 413 limit. Not tested: session expiry, and the browser-side validation that hides the server error.
evidence.ux_design: The pages look clean and consistent with a wine-coloured header and card layout (start.jpg) and a clear confirmation list (confirmation.jpg). The staff tables are tidy and show seats left for each tasting (staff.jpg). Weaknesses: 'Book …' is a small default-blue underlined link rather than a clear call-to-action button (start.jpg). After an invalid email, form.jpg shows no visible feedback, because only a temporary browser popup appears. There is no 'fully booked' state, no sign-out, and Cancel deletes a booking with no confirmation step.
evidence.accessibility: The page has lang="en" and a viewport meta tag. Each input is wrapped in its label, so it has an accessible name (views.js:78-86). Errors use role="alert" (views.js:68). Headings follow a sensible h1/h2 order, the staff table has a thead, and the confirmation uses dl/dt/dd. Text contrast is good (#222/#555 on light backgrounds, white on #4a1d2e). Gaps: no aria-invalid or aria-describedby linking the error to its field, focus does not move to the error, every row's Cancel button has the same accessible name with no booking context, the action column has an empty <th> (views.js:157), and there are no custom focus styles.
evidence.simplicity: There are no runtime dependencies: it uses only node:http and node:crypto (package.json has no dependencies). About 470 lines of source code across 4 files, which suits the brief. HTML is built with template strings and there is no framework.

unmet_requirements: Partly met: 'Invalid input is rejected with an error message next to the form'. In a browser, type="email" required (views.js:82) makes the browser block the submit, so the server's error message never shows; form.jpg shows the invalid email with no visible error.
strengths: Booking logic is correct, in one place, and synchronous: seat limits including exact fill, strict guest parsing, and cancelling frees seats (store.js:14-86).

Security is solid for the scope: every output is escaped, the password check is constant-time, session tokens are random, stored server-side and expire, the cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, request bodies are capped, and pages send a CSP (app.js, views.js).
Thorough HTTP-level and store-level tests cover every brief requirement plus XSS, auth refusal and oversized bodies, and the app has no dependencies.
issues: Browser validation (type=email, required, min/max) stops the submit, so the brief's 'error message next to the form' is never shown; form.jpg shows no visible error after an invalid email.
Staff authentication has no login rate limit, no sign-out and no Secure cookie flag, and Cancel deletes a booking immediately with no confirmation.

Accessibility and UX gaps: the error is not linked to its field (no aria-invalid or aria-describedby), every Cancel button has the same name, 'Book …' is a small plain link, and fully booked tastings still show a Book link.
review.verdict: This is a clean, dependency-free and well-tested booking app with correct seat logic, sound staff authentication and consistent output escaping. Before shipping, it needs one fix: guests must see the error message next to the form, which browser validation currently hides. A sign-out and a login rate limit would also be good to add.
